chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad and Fudaylah from Aban ibn Uthman from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sale of fodder when it is flowing water (sayh), where a man directs the water to his land, channels it to irrigate the grass, and he is the one who dug the river, owns the water, and plants whatever he wishes with it. He said: 'If the water belongs to him, he may plant whatever he wishes with it, and let him give charity of whatever he wishes.'
He said: And I asked him about the sale of the harvests of wheat and barley and other harvests. He said: 'It is permissible, so let him sell it if he wishes.'

key_terms.سَيْحاً: Flowing water (specifically from a river or channel)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on selling water and crops when one owns both the water source and the land?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the property rights of the water owner (malik al-ma') to sell both the water itself and the resulting harvests, emphasizing that ownership grants full discretion over usage and disposal. The Imam’s instruction to 'give charity as he wishes' highlights the voluntary nature of *sadaqah* in this context, distinguishing it from obligatory *zakat* on specific agricultural thresholds. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Islamic commercial law regarding private resources, allowing the owner to maximize benefit while retaining the spiritual option of voluntary giving.
